title: How to Plan for Retirement When You Want to Travel Full-Time
description: Budgeting for the 'Nomad' lifestyle: RVs, boats, and international living.
content:
Many retirees dream of selling the house and seeing the world. Whether it is 'Van Life', living on a boat, or slow-traveling through Europe via Airbnbs, a full-time travel retirement requires a specialized financial plan. You are trading fixed costs (Mortgage/Property Tax) for variable costs (Fuel/Flights/Lodging). This lifestyle can be cheaper than a stationary retirement (Geo-Arbitrage) or much more expensive depending on your pace. This guide builds the budget for a life on the move.

Key Takeaways

  • The 'Pace' Variable: Moving fast is expensive (daily flights/hotels). Moving slow is cheap (monthly Airbnb discounts). A 'Slow Travel' budget is often 30-40% lower than a 'Fast Travel' budget.
  • The 'Home Base' Cost: Do you keep a house? Maintaining a vacant home while traveling is a massive wealth drag. Renting it out or selling it releases capital to fund the travel.
  • Healthcare Logistics: Medicare does not cover you outside the US. You need Expat Health Insurance or a robust Travel Medical policy. Budget $300-$800/mo for this.
  • The 'Exit Strategy': You won't travel forever. You need a plan for age 80. Set aside a portion of your nest egg to buy back into the housing market or pay for a CCRC when you settle down.

Why It Matters (US Context)

Domicile is critical. If you sell your house and live in an RV, you still need a legal state of residence for taxes, voting, and driver's licenses. States like Florida, Texas, and South Dakota are popular for nomads due to 0% income tax and easy mail forwarding rules.

The Nomad Budget Builder

Scenario: Couple, Age 62. International Slow Travel.

1. Housing (The Arbitrage)

US Cost: $3,000/mo (Mortgage/Tax/Util).
Travel Cost: $2,000/mo (Airbnb monthly rates in Portugal/Thailand/Mexico).
Savings: $1,000/month.

2. Transportation

US Cost: $1,000/mo (2 Cars + Ins + Gas).
Travel Cost: $500/mo (Uber/Trains/Flights).
Savings: $500/month.

3. Food & Fun

US Cost: $1,000/mo.
Travel Cost: $1,500/mo (Eating out more).
Cost Increase: $500/month.

The Verdict: Full-time travel can be $1,000/mo cheaper than staying home, provided you stay in LCOL areas and move slowly.

Logistical Setup

  1. Establish Domicile: Pick a state (SD/FL/TX). Use a service like 'Escapees' or 'Dakota Post' to get a physical address, mail forwarding, and vehicle registration.
  2. Bank Accounts: Get a Schwab Investor Checking account. It refunds all ATM fees globally. You cannot travel without this.
  3. The 'Storage' Audit: Don't pay $300/mo for a storage unit for 10 years. That is $36,000. Sell the stuff. Buy new stuff if/when you settle down. Travel light.
  4. Phone Plans: Google Fi or T-Mobile allow international data. Or use local SIM cards (eSIMs) for cheaper rates.

Frequently Asked Questions

What about Medicare?

Keep Part A (Free). You might pay Part B premiums just to keep it active for when you return. Rely on private travel insurance while abroad.

Is RV life cheaper?

Not always. Gas, campsites ($50-$100/night), and repairs add up. 'Boondocking' (free camping) is cheap, but requires expensive solar/battery setups. RVing is a lifestyle choice, not always a savings strategy.

How do I get mail?

Mail forwarding services scan your mail to an app. You read it online. They shred junk and forward checks/cards to your current location.
